Primary Care Physician, Karen Vance, MD, dated 7/19/13: speech and language, social skills, sensory issues, cognitive delay (problem solving), and aggression. CONCERNS OF PARENTS:
Behavior: Slow to react with directions/commands, sensory issues (e.g. sensitive to loud noises or temperature changes), toe walking, and meltdowns 2-5 times per week (screaming, hitting hair/bed, inconsolable).She is quiet, less engaging in group activities, focused for initial part then unengaged and fidgety. Safety is a concern as she has poor awareness of danger, she will climb/ jumps excessively and will wander away in public
Development: delays in speech and languages and suspected delays in overall cognitive development
-Developmental milestones: history of early milestones is not available
Gross motor: she was walking at 19 months of age, she can now walk, run and climb stairs, she is often klutzy and will fall easily, she is very active
Fine motor: Right handed, good pencil grip uses utensils like spoon and fork with much
spillage, she can drink from an open cup with spillage, she can take off all clothes and will try to dress herself.
Speech and language: at 3 years she had only 1 word, now she has more than a 100 words in
English and will combine 2�3 words. She uses words to get needs met about 50 % of the time, the rest she will whine or cry. She can follow single step commands. Emma Rose Callahan attends the Sunshine Bilingual Chinese/ English preschool but care providers there are mainly Chinese speaking and so are the children. Emma Rose Callahan does not speak any Chinese.
Social interactions and Play: she does not seek out peers for play and prefers to parallel vs. joint play, others have to initiate play for her to join them, and �he enjoys pretending with her dolls. No atypical play was reported. She does not seem to seek out physical aff_ection often, but will go to her Mother for help and sometimes to tell her she loves her.
Self care: she wants to be very independent and likes to learn to do things for herself
Feeding: No history of difficulties with chewing, swallowing, choking, gagging or vomiting. She has a good appetite.
Sensory: sensitive to noise, she will cling to Mother if she hears loud noises eg: public toilet flushes,
she does not like her hair brushed but also does not like it touching her face, she does not like shampoos, baths , she tolerates tags and clothing textures and she often toe walks
Elimination: No history of chronic constipation or diarrhea. She has regular Bowel Movements; she is toilet trained but needs reminders to go to the bathroom. She is starting to let parents know that she has to use the bathroom more often now. She is dry most nights.

PSYCHOLOGY TESTS:
WPPSI-IV: The Wechsler Preschool & Primary Scale of Intelligence - Fourth Edition, is an individually administered test to evaluate the verbal and nonverbal skills of children ranging in age from 2.6 to 3.11 years. Verbal skills include pointing to requested pictures and nonverbal skills are putting puzzles together and blocks into various designs. Emma Rose Callahan received the following scores with scores between 90 - 110 and 8 � 12 considered within the Average range.

Behavioral Observat;ons: Emma Rose Callahan completed the WPPSI-IV.	Though she was able to comply with directions, Emma Rose Callahan required motivation to participate in some tasks. She required only some redirection back to tasks.	She appeared motivated by verbal praise and sticker reinforcers.  Emma Rose Callahan exhibited some hypersensitivity to tactile stimuli; when she earned a sticker, she went to her adoptive mother and stuck it on her adoptive mother's skin.  With accommodations, she was able to maintain good attention to tasks.  When her energy level was heightened, she appeared more engaged in the activity than when she was asked to sit at the table and engage.
Verbal Comprehens;on Index: Emma Rose Callahan's performance varied significantly. She scored in the Average
range on the Receptive Vocabulary subtest; this assesses one's ability to identify the correct picture in an array of pictures (e.g., Show me snowing). Emma Rose Callahan scored in the Low Average range on the Information subtest; which assesses one's ability to provide responses to general knowledge questions (e.g., What color is the sun?). Emma Rose Callahan scored in the Average range on the Picture Naming supplemental subtest; indicating slight delays in her expressive language.
Visual Spatial Index. Emma Rose Callahan's performance varied significantly. She scored in the Average range, at
age expectancy, on the Block Design subtest; this subtest measures one's ability to efficiently visually deconstruct and manually reconstruct an image using blocks. Emma Rose Callahan scored in the Low Average range on the Object Assembly subtest; which measures one's ability to integrate pieces into a whole.
Working Memory Index: Emma Rose Callahan's performance varied significantly.	She scored in the Average range
on the Picture Memory task. This suggests that her visual memory is at age expectancy. Emma Rose Callahan performed in the Average range on the Zoo Locations subtest. This indicates that her ability to recall placement of meaningful images is at age expectancy.
Summary: There was a significant split between domain scores on the WPPSI-IV; therefore the Full
Scale IQ score should be interpreted with some caution. Emma Rose Callahan showed a relative strength in her ability to correctly identify pictures when asked to pick one out (e.g. Show me snowing). She showed a relative weakness in a visually-based task which requires putting together puzzle pieces.

REHABILITATION SPECIALIST TESTS (SENSORY MOTOR)
Sensory Profile: The Sensory Profile is a parent report measure to capture a child's reaction to and seeking of various sensory experiences. Emma Rose Callahan's adoptive mother filled out the Sensory Profile. On this parent checklist a child can fall into three categories:
Typical Performance which indicates that a child is processing information in a way that is typical of
children her age; Probable Difference meaning that in some areas a child is processing information differently than her peers; Definite Difference indicates that a child is processing information differently than her peers in most areas. Emma Rose Callahan scored as follows:

These scores are consistent with what was seen in clinic today. Emma Rose Callahan is showing significant signs of sensory processing difficulties.	Areas that she struggles with are indicated in the chart above reflecting definite differences from how her peers respond to sensory input.	Specific examples seen today are: preferring to complete tasks such as putting on her shoes and balancing on a therapy ball by herself rather than having hands on assistance.	Leaving the testing area and seeking out multiple opportunities to play on uneven surfaces and to climb up on furniture and high surfaces, and; having
difficulty sustaining her attention to tasks when her arousal/attention level was low. Emma Rose Callahan benefits	I
from sensory movement breaks to help her sustain attention.

Fine Motor: Emma Rose Callahan is meeting developmental milestones for fine motor skills for her age. Her fine motor skills fell in theaverage to above average range. She was able to demonstrate the following skills today in clinic: tracing a line (41-42 month level), copy a cross (39-40 month level), and lace a string (39-40 month level). She has a dominant (right) hand, uses a mature 3-finger grip on a marker or pencil, uses her non-dominant hand to assist during fine motor tasks (i.e., stabilize the paper), and snips with scissors. She buttons (47-48 month level) and unbuttons (41-42 month level) 1-inch buttons.

Gross Motor: Emma Rose Callahan is meeting developmental milestones in gross motor skills for her age. Her gross motor skills fell well within the average range. She moves in a fairly well coordinated manner; however she frequently loses her balance, trips over her feet and occasionally falls. Currently, Emma Rose Callahan is able to: jump hurdles (33-34 month level), walk on tiptoes (29-30 month level), walk up stairs placing 1 foot on each step while holding the railing. She lost her balance and almost fell while descending stairs, and her adoptive mother reports that Emma Rose Callahan falls frequently at home.	Emma Rose Callahan has difficulty balancing on one foot and placing her arms correctly in front of her body to catch a playground size ball (33-34 month level).

Self Care/Adaptive: Emma Rose Callahan is meeting many age appropriate self care skills. She is toilet trained during the day, yet has frequent accidents.	She sleeps in a pull-up and is usually dry in the morning. Emma Rose Callahan is feeding herself using primarily utensils or finger feeding. She has difficulty getting food to her mouth with a spoon. She can drink from an open cup with some spilling.	Her adoptive mother reports that Emma Rose Callahan is able to dress herself except for managing fasteners such as buttons. She is able to unzip a
z1• pper.
DIAGNOSTIC FINDINGS: Emma Rose Callahan is a delightful 3-year-old old Caucasian girl.  Her developmental history is remarkable for exposure to trauma. Her medical history is remarkable for alleged in utero exposure to methamphetamines. She has been in the care of her adoptive family for approximately 18 months. She was referred by her pediatrician for concerns regarding sensory issues, suspected cognitive delays, speech and language delays, social skills, and severe aggression (mostly during meltdowns).

Cognitive skills tested using the Wechsler Preschool ft Primary Scale of Intelligence (WPPSI-IV) showed that her performance varied significantly within subtests, but she demonstrated Average abilities in all
areas.
Emma Rose Callahan's history is remarkable for exposure to trauma. Findings from the CBCL s.howed clinically significant withdrawal and somatic complaints. Her adoptive mother also reported that Emma Rose Callahan

experiences meltdowns 2-5 times per week during which she screams, hits furniture, and is difficult to console. She was observed during testing to have lower energy and a slight affect, engaging more fully when prompted to be at a higher energy level. At times, she appeared withdrawn. She required prompts and motivators. Emma Rose Callahan has progressed developmentally since being in the care of her adoptive parents; however, she is still experiencing symptoms related to her history of trauma. These difficulties meet the criteria for Adjustment Disorder with Depressed Mood (309.0) (this subtype is used for responses that are predominantly with a depressed mood) per the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fourth Edition, Text Revision (DSM-IV-TR).

On standardized sensory and motor evaluation measures, Emma Rose Callahan demonstrates above average fine motor skills, and visual motor and gross motor skills well within the average range.  She was able to do well on tasks such as drawing, cutting, and buttoning, as well as on tasks like running, jumping, and climbing stairs.	She scored as having difficulties processing sensory information in most areas on the Sensory Profile. This means that she has trouble processing information coming through her senses, such as tactile or auditory information, which results in behaviors such as avoiding sensory input, seeking out more sensory information, missing important sensory information in the environment, or having difficulty transitioning between sedentary tasks and movement tasks.

Etiology of her condition is unknown but unknown genetic loading,	prenatal exposure to toxins and history of neglect may be contributory factors. Emma Rose Callahan does not meet criteria for a full Fetal Alcohol Syndrome {FAS) diagnosis. Her prenatal growth history is unknown, her current growth percentiles are
> 50th percentile, she has a fairly well formed philtrum and a normal vermillion (upper lip) without small palpebral fissures and hence does not have all 3 FAS features. The effects of prenatal methamphetamine exposure may contribute to developmental and behavioral problems, but research has been inconsistent as to its effects.

CHILD-FAMILY STRENGTHS: Emma Rose Callahan is a friendly and social girl who has made great progress in her develop111ent since living with her adoptive parents. Her family is supportive, active in her life and willing to work with her to help her succeed.
RECOMMENDATIONS:
Primary Care Physician is encouraged to continue to monitor health, growth, developmental and behavioral progress, contacting KidScope's nurse Abby at 408-555-0170 if  new concerns not addressed in this report warrant further assessment or intervention. Please follow-up on:

Therapy if she complains of feet pain or continues to fall often during gross motor activites

Given recent move of residences, it is recommended that Parents Helping Parents assist family with transitional services and/or with initiation of Individualized Education Program or accommodations, as
needed.

It is recommended that Emma Rose Callahan be re-evaluated in approximately 12 to 18 months from the date of this evaluation after receiving therapeutic services.	The purpose of the re-evaluation will be to re­ assess Hanf)a 's level of functioning, for diagnostic clarification, and to gain updated treatment recommendations.

In order to better understand sensory processing, it is recomn1ended that Emma Rose Callahan's caregivers read the books, The Out of Sync Cl1ild, and T/1e Out of Sync Child Has Fun, by Carol Stock Kranowitz.  They can be found at the public library, on A111azon.com, and at large bookstores, such as Barnes & Noble.	An additional book that may be helpful is: Raising a Sensory Smart Child: The Definitive Handbook for Helping Your Child with Sensory Processing Issues, by Lindsey Biel M.A, OTR/L and Nancy Peske, published in 2009 by Penguin Books.	In order to help Emma Rose Callahan return to a calm and focused state, it is recommended that her caregivers provide opportunities for "heavy work", which can include having Emma Rose Callahan move furniture, carry a weighted backpack on walks or pull a weighted down wagon on walks.
